title: Edge TLS rehandshake cascade — P1 hosted API incident postmortem
content:
Summary:

On 2026-03-19 between ~18:04 and 18:42 UTC the hosted API experienced increased 5xx rates and elevated tail latency for streaming and short-text generation routes. Impact: ~14% of requests returned 5xx (mostly 502/504) and median p99 latency increased from ~120ms to ~1.8s for affected routes. No data exfiltration. Total customer-facing window ~38 minutes with partial recovery after manual mitigation. Severity: P1 (service degraded, significant customer impact to streaming clients).

What happened (plain English):
An interaction between a recently deployed change to edge TLS session handling and a spike in client connection churn caused our edge proxies to perform repeated TLS rehandshakes. Rehandshakes caused worker thread saturation inside the proxy process and increased time spent waiting on socket handshakes, which in turn delayed request forwarding and caused connection timeouts to upstream compute pools. Several upstream pools returned connection errors under heavy backlog, producing 502/504s.

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 18:03:42 ALERT: grafana-alert edge-5xx-rate crossed threshold (anomaly detection)
- 18:04:05 Pager duty -> on-call SRE (Arjun) paged
- 18:05:10 Initial triage: spike in SYN/SSL activity shown on edge egress metrics; SYN rate up 3x baseline
- 18:06:00 Observed p99 TLS handshake duration climb from 8ms to 250ms on edge-proxy nodes
- 18:08:20 502/504 spike begins in hosted-api-prod (~12% 5xx)
- 18:12:00 Scoped to region-us-west-2 edge cluster (edge-cluster-7)
- 18:18:00 Mitigation 1: scaled edge-proxy deployment from 12 -> 24 replicas (manual kubectl scale)
- 18:22:30 Mitigation 2: applied transient iptables rule to drop repeated rehandshake traffic from abusive IP blocks (temporary stopgap)
- 18:28:00 Partial recovery noted (5xx reduced to ~4%)
- 18:42:00 System stabilized; monitoring continued for 3 hours

Root cause analysis:
Primary cause: regression in edge-proxy TLS session resumption logic introduced in PR #482 (changes to session cache eviction and new per-connection session ticket behavior). Under high connection churn, session resumption attempts failed more often causing full handshake fallbacks.
Contributing factors:
- Lower-than-expected session-ticket reuse due to the change in how tickets are marked stale (cache TTL miscalculation).
- Edge proxy's thread model prioritized connection accept over completing handshakes, allowing queue build-up of unfinished handshakes.
- No automatic fallback rule existed to route excess TLS-handshake-heavy traffic to a standby proxy tier.

Why didn't auto-scaling catch it sooner?
Horizontal autoscaler targets CPU but TLS handshakes were blocking in user-space and not always reflected as CPU spike (blocked syscalls). The manual scale helped but was slower than an ideal reactive mitigation.

Immediate mitigation steps performed: (what we did during incident)
- Brief: scale edge-proxy horizontally (kubectl scale deployment/edge-proxy -n edge 12 -> 24)
- Blacklist high-rate client IPs at iptables level on edge-cluster-7 to interrupt rehandshake storm
- Re-deployed previous edge-proxy image (rollback to v1.14.3) onto a canary subset of nodes to validate that rollback reduces handshake duration
- Opened traffic steering to fallback region for a small % of traffic (5%) to relieve pressure on us-west-2

Longer-term fixes proposed (with owners and target dates):
- Revert and patch session-ticket TTL logic in PR #482 (owner: Lucia Morales, due: 2026-03-26)
- Add a handshake-duration SLO and alert (owner: Ben O'Neill, due: 2026-04-02)
- Implement backlog-aware autoscaler metric (blocked-fds / handshake-queue-length) (owner: SRE infra team, due: 2026-05-01)
- Build an automatic traffic circuit-breaker that detects excessive TLS-handshake retries and routes to standby cluster (owner: Eng Proxy, due: 2026-05-15)
- Add unit/integration tests for session ticket resumption edge cases and simulate high churn (owner: Applied ML infra, due: 2026-04-10)

Runbook draft (new items to add to edge runbook):
- Detection: add metric `edge.tls.handshake_duration_p99` and alert on sustained >200ms for 3m
- Triage steps:
  1) Identify affected cluster: query grafana dashboard `edge-tps-and-errors` for server/region
  2) Check `ss -ntp | grep ESTAB` and `netstat` for high connection churn patterns
  3) Run `kubectl get pods -n edge -o wide` to find node saturation
- Immediate mitigations:
  - `kubectl scale deployment/edge-proxy -n edge --replicas=<current*2>`
  - `kubectl rollout undo deployment/edge-proxy -n edge --to-revision=<previous>` (if rollback validated)
  - On-call: run `sudo iptables -I INPUT -s <ip> -j DROP` for abusive IPs and log for remediation team
- Escalation: if >10% 5xx persists for >10m, page Eng Proxy and Product (CS) and consider partial traffic migration

On-call notes (commands run / observations captured):
- 18:05 arjun@oncall: ssh edge-cluster-7-proxy-3 -> ran `tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'` and observed SYN burst from ~120 unique /16 ranges
- 18:08 ran `openssl s_client -connect proxy:443 -tls1_2 -msg` and captured repeated FULL handshakes vs session reuse
- 18:15 `kubectl get hpa -n edge` showed no change; HPA configured on CPU only
- 18:18 `kubectl scale deployment/edge-proxy -n edge --replicas=24` (effects visible ~3m later)
- 18:22 set temporary iptables drops on 8 candidate IP blocks (audit ticket JIRA-2021 opened to review)

Lessons learned:
- Testing: Session cache edge-cases were not covered by integration tests that simulate massive connection churn; add load tests that specifically exercise TLS resumption behavior.
- Monitoring: CPU-only autoscaling missed a starvation mode; we need metrics for blocked syscalls and handshake queue depth.
- Runbook: insufficient guidance on when to deploy iptables blocks vs. rollback; add explicit decision tree.
- Release process: any change touching TLS/session-ticket handling should require a canary in low-traffic region for 48h with synthetic churn test.

Action items (owner / ETA / status):
- Lucia Morales — revert session-ticket TTL bug and PR with unit tests — due 2026-03-26 — open
- Ben O'Neill — add handshake-duration SLO + grafana alert — due 2026-04-02 — in_progress
- Arjun Kapoor — update edge runbook with triage and iptables decision tree — due 2026-04-06 — in_progress
- SRE infra — prototype backlog-aware HPA metric (handshake queue length exporter) — due 2026-05-01 — planned
- Applied ML infra — create integration test harness for connection churn and TLS resumption — due 2026-04-10 — planned

Appendix (raw metrics & notes):
- Grafana snapshots attached in linked_artifacts; key metrics: TLS handshake p99, accept queue length, edge tps, upstream error rate
- Incident Slack thread: linked_artifacts
- Preliminary root cause label: code-regression (edge-proxy PR #482) + insufficient autoscaling signal

If anything in this doc needs correction or you have additional on-call logs, paste them into the Slack thread and I will incorporate them before finalizing the postmortem.
